review_cost.rationale: One round of nits (wildcard hosts, duplicated team-query builder, unused dependency, nav error handler) — nothing requiring structural rework; I'd approve after those are addressed or acknowledged.

findings.issue: allowedHosts: ['*'] deviates from Angular SSR guidance, which says not to use a wildcard unless a trusted proxy validates forwarded headers.
findings.suggestion: Configure an explicit host list from the environment (or document the trusted-proxy assumption); the comment shows awareness, so at minimum make it configurable.

findings.issue: Server state comes from a 1-year cookie, client state from localStorage; when they diverge (localStorage cleared, cookie kept), SSR DOM differs from the hydrated render (team button label, team page content) causing a hydration mismatch error.
findings.suggestion: On first browser load, sync the cookie unconditionally (overwrite even when the stored team is empty), or accept a `withNoHttpTransferCache`-style re-render path for the team page.

findings.issue: A failed fetch rejects the route resolver; with no withNavigationErrorHandler the failed client-side navigation silently leaves the previous page rendered.
findings.suggestion: Add a global navigation error handler that shows an error state or retries, per the data-resolvers guidance.

findings.issue: The `names=` query string for the team page-data path is built twice (resolver and team-page.ts load()), so the two can drift.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single teamPath(names) helper next to the VM definition.

findings.issue: Manual effect + loadId race guard + linkedSignal seeding re-implements what resource() (params: team names, loader: PageData) provides with built-in abort/status handling.
findings.suggestion: Model the team view model as a resource, or keep the manual version but note why resource() wasn't used (initial input seeding from the resolver).

findings.issue: withEventReplay() is redundant in Angular 22: provideClientHydration() enables event replay and incremental hydration by default.
findings.suggestion: Drop the argument (provideClientHydration()) — it also removes a stale-looking reference that will need cleanup.

findings.issue: Scroll restoration is hand-rolled (subscription + previous-URL tracking + afterNextRender) instead of withInMemoryScrolling defaults; correct, but it's custom state the router could own if defaults allowed query-only navigations to keep position.
findings.suggestion: Keep it, but document the specific router behavior being worked around, or track the upstream router option that fixes it.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is a declared dependency but never imported.
Module-level clientCache is hidden global state with a TTL but no size bound; fine in practice, but it's invisible to anyone debugging stale data.
findings.suggestion: Either bound it like the server cache (MAX_ENTRIES) or move it behind the PAGE_DATA_LOADER provider with a comment describing the TTL semantics.

summary: A polished, current-with-Angular-22 app: signal-based components, resolver-plus-input-binding data flow, correct SSR/hydration wiring, good a11y and naming, with why-comments and a README that explain the architecture. The main trade-off to own as a team is the custom view-model data layer (server loaders + /_data + TransferState) that bypasses HttpClient/resource in exchange for small payloads, plus a handful of minor edge-case risks. I'd merge after one round of nits; nothing requires structural rework.
